- Deliver clear handoff materials and a playbook for transition to an AE or an ongoing hire.
- Coordinate closely with the founder or sole executive stakeholder throughout the engagement; focus on build, validate, and enable — not long-term sales management.
- Recommend tooling and operations improvements and optimize CRM/outbound tool usage; manage reasonable outbound tooling month-to-month (budget available).

- Proven RevOps / sales-ops / sales-enablement experience that includes building an outbound motion from near-zero — ideally at a consulting/implementation/services firm or large professional services organization.

### Role Summary

We are looking for a **GTM Engineer** to build the AI and automation that make ClickHouse's go-to-market motion faster, smarter, and more scalable. This is a builder role. You will design, build, and ship the systems, agents, and workflows that take manual work off the team and put usage and customer signals to work across the lifecycle. ClickHouse runs on a consumption model, where the returns from instrumenting and automating the customer journey are large and mostly uncaptured. This role exists to capture them.

### Responsibilities

- Design, build, and ship AI and automation across the GTM motion: prospecting and enrichment, lead routing and activation, outbound and follow-up, deal and technical sales support, and expansion and retention signals.
- Build agents and workflows that run reliably at scale and take repetitive work off Sales, Solutions Architecture, and Marketing.
- Instrument the customer lifecycle. Connect the GTM systems and data so usage and telemetry signals flow to the right place and trigger the right action automatically.
- Partner with the field to find where AI and automation create real gains, and turn those opportunities into systems people actually use.
- Own what you build end-to-end. Design it, deploy it, measure whether it moves a real number, and keep improving it. Stand up evals and monitoring so AI output stays reliable in production.
- Set the standards and guardrails for AI in GTM: data quality, prompt and eval discipline, human review where it matters, and controls that keep automated actions safe.
- Track the AI and automation tooling landscape and bring the best of it into how ClickHouse goes to market.

### Requirements/Qualifications

- 5+ years building automation and tooling in a GTM, RevOps, or growth engineering context, with systems you have shipped and run in production.
- Production experience with the GTM stack: Salesforce as the system of record, Gong and Gong Engage for conversation intelligence and sequencing, and the engineering layer beneath them: Vercel, Clay, n8n, enrichment providers, and both transactional and analytical databases (Postgres and ClickHouse). You have shipped and operated these in production at real scale.
- Hands-on development in Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript.
- Fluency with modern AI tooling: LLM APIs, agent and orchestration frameworks, prompting, evals, and retrieval with embeddings and vector search. You know how to get reliable behavior out of probabilistic systems, and you use eval and observability tooling like Langfuse to keep them reliable in production.
- Strong data-activation skills: SQL, APIs, and integrations, transformation with dbt, and moving warehouse data into the GTM stack and back.
- A builder who ships. You are comfortable owning something from idea to working system, and you measure it by whether it runs reliably and moves a real number.
- Owner-operator mindset. You treat what you build as a system you own end-to-end: you build it, you run it, you fix it when it breaks, and you keep making it better.
- Judgment about where AI and automation help and where they create risk. You know when to automate a workflow fully, when to keep a human in the loop, and when to leave a process alone.
- Familiarity with usage-based or consumption-based business models is a plus. You understand how usage and telemetry signals drive expansion and retention.
- Strong written and verbal communication. Comfortable partnering across the field and explaining what your systems do and why.
- Bachelor's degree in engineering required. A master's degree is a plus.

### Compensation

For roles based in the **United States**, the typical starting salary range for this position is $145,000 - $195,000 USD. In certain locations, such as the San Francisco Bay Area and the New York City Metro Area, a premium market range may apply, as listed. These salary ranges reflect what we reasonably and in good faith believe to be the minimum and maximum pay for this role at the time of posting. The actual compensation may be higher or lower than the amounts listed, and the ranges may be subject to future adjustments. An individual’s placement within the range will depend on various factors, including (but not limited to) education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, location, performance, and the needs of the business or organization.

### Location/Workplace Type

Remote-friendly. ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and currently operates in over 20 countries.

# GTM Engineer
## Location
In person in New York City

## Employment Type
Full time

## Location Type
On-site

## What we're building
Mutiny is the self-improving AI infrastructure for GTM teams to execute faster and close more revenue. With Mutiny, everyone in sales and marketing gets a bench of GTM athletes that handle any work across their revenue motion and learn from what's actually moved their deals.

## The opportunity
Most GTM engineers wire up someone else's stack. You'll build a new one. As Mutiny's GTM engineer, you'll own the systems that power how we go to market, from outbound and onboarding to enrichment, routing, and the AI-native workflows that let a small team operate like a much bigger one. This role is in person in New York City, five days a week.

## What you'll own
- **Automations and internal tools.** Build the workflows and tools that make sales and marketing faster. The tool you ship today saves the team a week next month.
- **The plumbing.** APIs, data flows, integrations between every tool we run on. You make systems talk so the team doesn't have to.

## Who you are
- **A systems thinker.** You see one-off work and want to make it repeatable. You spot patterns and bottlenecks before they become someone's full-time problem.
- **A builder.** You've shipped automations, internal tools, and workflows that made a team measurably faster. You'd rather build than brief.
- **Comfortable with plumbing.** APIs, data flows, enrichment, routing. You know how to connect systems and make them work, even when the docs are wrong.
- **A cross-functional translator.** You can explain what you're building and why it matters to a CMO, a CRO, and an engineer in the same week. None of them feel talked down to.

Compensation Range: $150K - $250K

**Job Title:** Founding US Solutions Engineer

**Location:** New York City (On-Site)

**Compensation:** $180-220k OTE (uncapped) + Equity

**About Kombo:**
Kombo is the unified API for HR, payroll, Assessment, LMS and recruiting systems. Instead of spending months building integrations one by one, companies integrate once with Kombo and connect to 120+ platforms instantly.

**The Role:**
We're hiring our first US-based Solutions Engineer to own the technical relationship with customers - from first sales call through to successful implementation. You'll be the technical expert prospects and customers rely on to understand how Kombo fits their stack, design their integration approach, and get them live. You'll work closely with our Sales team, and our CRO to close deals and with Product/Engineering to turn customer insights into product improvements. This is a builder role. You'll help establish our US solutions team, create repeatable playbooks, and shape how we work with customers.

**Responsibilities:**
- **Own the technical sales cycle:** Lead discovery and demos, translating customer requirements into integration designs; Create technical proposals covering architecture, security, and implementation approach; Partner with AEs to close complex deals with engineering and executive stakeholders.
- **Drive implementations to go-live:** Own the technical relationship from POC to signed contract through production deployment; Build implementation plans, troubleshoot API issues, and unblock customers directly; Serve as the escalation point until customers are live and successful.
- **Build the technical toolkit:** Create demo environments, code samples (Python, Node.js), and Postman collections; Write integration guides, architecture diagrams, and troubleshooting documentation; Develop sales collateral: security questionnaire responses to technical one-pagers.
- **Scale the US solutions function:** Document repeatable playbooks for discovery, scoping, and implementation; Feed customer insights to Product/Engineering to shape the roadmap; Help define hiring and onboarding as we grow the team.

**Requirements/Qualifications:**
- 4+ years in Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or technical customer-facing roles at a B2B SaaS company.
- Hands-on experience with APIs - you can read documentation, write sample code, and debug integration issues.
- Track record working complex deals with technical and non-technical stakeholders - consistent deal value of $100k-150k+.
- Strong communication skills: you can whiteboard architecture with engineers and explain value to executives.
- Comfort with ambiguity and building things from scratch.

**Compensation:** $180-220k OTE (uncapped) + Equity

**Location/Workplace Type:** New York City (On-Site) 4+ days per week.

**Go-to-Market Engineer**

Revivn is a profitable and rapidly growing company that helps enterprises manage their technology through our end of life software platform. We take electronic recycling one step further by repurposing hardware that still has remaining life and providing it to people who lack dedicated computer access and make it more affordable for people who may not be able to purchase new technology. Working with companies like Instacart, Lyft, Qualtrics, X, Gensler, and Allbirds we are changing the way companies view used technology with a new model that focuses on repurposing instead of recycling.

We’re hiring our first Go-to-Market Engineer: a creative builder who sits between RevOps, marketing and full-stack engineering. Maybe you’re a computer science grad or early-career engineer who loves experimenting with tools and automation but doesn’t want to get lost in a giant company. You want to see the impact of what you build every day — on real leads, data, and revenue.

This is a hybrid technical + commercial role — ideal for someone who loves hacking together systems, writing quick scripts, and making data come alive. You’ll report into Marketing and collaborate closely with RevOps, Data, and Sales to automate workflows, enrich data, and make our GTM machine smarter, faster, and more creative.

**What You’ll Do**
- Build, scrape, and automate: Own the GTM automation and enrichment stack — from web scraping (Apify) to AI-driven enrichment (Hugging Face).
- Connect and create: Use APIs and lightweight code (Python, JavaScript) to glue together tools and make our data flow effortlessly.
- Experiment fast: Prototype workflows, test ideas, and turn what works into repeatable playbooks.
- Work across teams: Collaborate with Marketing, RevOps, and Sales to translate messy problems into automated systems.
- Push boundaries: Play with libraries like Crawlee, Cheerio, BeautifulSoup, Transformers, and Datasets to make research and enrichment faster.
- Stay curious: Constantly explore new AI, no-code, and automation tools — from Make and Zapier to emerging scrapers and APIs.
- Make GTM scale creatively: Build automations that still feel human — thoughtful, personal, and scalable.

**Who You Are**
- Creative problem-solver — you love finding clever shortcuts and unconventional ways to get things done.
- Early-career engineer, ideally with a CS or data-focused background, and eager to grow.
- In-between RevOps and full-stack: technical enough to code, curious enough to understand business context.
- Excited about tools: you tinker with APIs, scrape sites for fun, or wire up automations just to see what’s possible.
- Comfortable with ambiguity: you can turn loose ideas into structured systems.
- Fast learner and builder: you ship things quickly, break them, fix them, and learn.
- Motivated by impact: you want to see your work directly influence growth, pipeline, and revenue.

**Tech Stack**
- Languages: Python, JavaScript
- Web scraping: Apify, Crawlee, Cheerio, BeautifulSoup
- AI enrichment: Hugging Face, Transformers, Datasets
- Automation: Zapier, Make, Clay
- CRM and GTM stack: Salesforce, plus whatever creative tools you bring to the table.

**Perks**
- Competitive salary
- Direct impact: your work fuels meetings, pipeline, and revenue
- Ownership: this is a role built from the ground up – you’ll shape how GTM at Revivn evolves
- Growth environment: scrappy, fast-paced, feedback driven
- Collaboration with Sales, Data, RevOps, Engineering

If this sounds like you, apply! If you don’t meet all of the qualifications but think you could be a match, we’d still love the chance to review your application.

We embrace diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive environment. At Revivn, we encourage people from all ages, abilities, and experiences to apply. Revivn does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or family status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, pregnancy or caregiver status, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

At Revivn, we prioritize transparency about our salary throughout the entire recruitment process. Be prepared to chat about compensation on your initial screen so that we can ensure alignment. If salary expectations and ranges are out of sync, we believe it is kind to respect everyone’s time and may discontinue conversations.

But, here at Revivn, we ALSO believe in investing in the lifetime value of each individual we meet and interact with. (We love knowing good humans and supporting them in whatever they do). We know that if it isn’t a good fit at the moment, it doesn’t necessarily mean that it won’t be a good fit in the future as we both continue to grow! We work to remain in contact with prospective candidates if the recruitment process ends early on.

For all job openings, we consider candidates with various backgrounds and levels of experience. When we give an offer it is based on individual skills and experience, as well as how that stacks up against other employees in the role. The salary range for a Go-to-Market Engineer is expected to be between **$85,000-120,000/year**. Your exact offer may vary based on these factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, and experience. The compensation package will also include comprehensive benefits such as medical, dental, and vision coverage, along with a 401(k) plan.

What Is a Career Ladder?

A career ladder, or career path, is a progression framework. It allows an organization to describe the different job levels and the expectations for a given position.

It enables the assessment of a software engineer's skills and to work on her career progression. It provides a shared framework to identify the different aspects to improve to reach the next job level.

The ladder can also be mapped with employee's compensation, increasing salaries transparency, and fairness.

Expertise Path and Manager Path (Dual-Track)

Most of the software engineering career ladders are dual tracks ladders.

They have a joint base for the first positions, and at some point, two paths are possible the expertise path and the people management path. The expertise path is often named the individual contributor track, the people management path is often called the manager track.

Mar 26 Sharing Our Engineering Ladder

Camille

I gave a talk last year at the NYC CTO summit on how and why to introduce structure into an engineering organization (slides available here). I am a fan of structure and the clarity that it can provide an organization, despite its potential downsides. I'm not going to talk about the WHY very much in this post, but I thought it was about time that I helped with the HOW.

Creating an engineering ladder (that is, the job descriptions and levels of an engineering organization) is a daunting task. If you do a half-hearted job, you're likely to cause more problems than you solve. The very first ladder I presented to my team was based on the ladder at Foursquare*. It was very simple, with one or two descriptive elements per "attribute" of engineering (technical skill, communication skill, etc), and by all accounts worked very well for their team. I hoped that this style of providing fewer details would result in people being less obsessed with the ladder, less likely to try to negotiate their level on "technicalities". Boy was I wrong. Almost immediately I had engineers debating me over whether they were at the right level, and there was a great deal of anxiety and confusion throughout the organization. I left room for generous interpretation, and it made it difficult for me to explain what I really wanted and expected.

snippet:
**Role Summary:**
We're hiring a Go-To-Market (GTM) Engineer to join the Growth organization, where you'll work directly with Sales, Marketing, RevOps, and beyond to translate GTM strategy into action by building systems, running experiments, activating signals, and scaling what works. This is a hands-on systems role. You'll design and ship the data pipelines, automation systems, scoring models, and AI-assisted workflows that power how Immuta identifies, reaches, and converts enterprise buyers. You won't be handing off requirements to an engineering team — you'll be writing the code, wiring the integrations, and owning the output end-to-end.

**Core Responsibilities:**
- **Signal Aggregation & Scoring Systems**
  - Build and maintain ICP scoring models, intent signal pipelines, and account prioritization logic sourced across our stack (Salesforce, Apollo, Warmly, Clay, and more)
  - Own the data transformation layer: pulling from CRM, enrichment APIs, and intent platforms, normalizing and enriching, and writing clean outputs back to Salesforce or downstream activation tools
  - Partner with RevOps on data definitions and quality to ensure scoring logic runs on trustworthy inputs

- **AI-Assisted GTM Workflows**
  - Apply LLMs to automate research, contact enrichment, signal extraction, and outreach personalization at scale
  - Design workflows that are measurable, testable, and repeatable — not one-off prompts
  - Reduce manual effort across Sales and Marketing by replacing high-frequency, low-complexity tasks with reliable automation

- **Middleware & Integration Infrastructure**
  - Build lightweight orchestration systems that connect GTM tools across the stack
  - Own the full lifecycle: standing up, maintaining, and iterating on integrations as the tool stack evolves
  - Know when to use n8n vs a custom FastAPI endpoint vs a scheduled Python job, and implement whichever is right

- **Experimentation & Measurement**
  - Build the scaffolding that lets the team run GTM experiments across audiences, channels, and messaging
  - Instrument experiments with enough signals to distinguish what's working from what's noise
  - Operationalize successful approaches by moving from one-off test to repeatable, scalable system

**Requirements/Qualifications:**
- **Experience:** 5+ years in Sales Ops, GTM Ops, RevOps, Marketing Ops, or a related technical role
- **Python:** Proficiency with pandas, data transformation pipelines, scoring model construction, and structured output formatting — comfortable owning a codebase, not just running scripts
- **Integration Engineering:** Hands-on experience building systems that ingest data from multiple sources, apply transformation logic at a midpoint layer, and route outputs to a destination (Zapier, n8n, or custom API orchestration)
- **Salesforce:** Strong data fluency — you know the object model, can write SOQL, and understand how CRM data needs to be structured to be usable downstream
- **Problem Solving:** Experience translating open-ended business questions into working systems with minimal specification; consulting, agency, or early-stage SaaS backgrounds are a strong fit
- **LLMs:** Familiarity with LLMs in production contexts — classification, extraction, summarization, and prompt chaining (not just vibe coding)

**Compensation:**
$115,000 - $140,000 a year. Additional compensation may include commission, variable pay, or equity, alongside benefits like healthcare, stock options, parental leave, unlimited paid time off, and learning resources.

**Location/Workplace Type:**
Austin, TX or Columbus, OH; Remote; Hybrid workplace.

snippet:
**About the Role**
As a GTM Engineer at Attentive, you will serve as an embedded technical builder within Revenue Operations, reporting to the VP of Revenue Operations. This role is designed to increase the speed, adaptability, and leverage of our go-to-market organization by building smart, lightweight solutions on top of our core systems landscape. You will partner closely with our RevTech team, which owns the foundational systems roadmap and long-term architecture, while operating in a distinct lane: moving quickly to solve high-value GTM problems that do not need to wait for the core roadmap. This includes designing and deploying fast, thoughtful solutions across workflow automation, data enrichment, AI-enabled processes, and bespoke internal tooling that reduce manual work and improve the quality of our go-to-market signals. This role is ideal for someone who is highly technical, pragmatic, and deeply motivated by shipping real solutions quickly. You should be excited by ambiguity, energized by business problems, and constantly looking for ways to make our teams faster, smarter, and more effective.

**What You’ll Accomplish**
- **Build fast, high-impact GTM solutions:** Design and ship workflows, automations, and internal tools that improve how our Sales and Customer Success teams operate day to day.
- **Reduce manual work across the GTM organization:** Eliminate repetitive rep and CSM tasks by automating data capture, field population, handoffs, enrichment, and workflow steps across tools like Salesforce, Gong, and other GTM systems.
- **Increase signal density and data usefulness:** Improve the quality of the data we collect and surface by auto-populating the fields that matter most, enriching customer and pipeline data, and making key signals easier for teams to act on.
- **Identify and deploy AI-enabled workflows:** Proactively explore how AI, agents, and automation platforms can improve go-to-market productivity, reduce operational burden, and create leverage before every underlying system is fully mature.
- **Operate with speed and pragmatism:** Build with a clear point of view on where speed matters most versus where durability and enterprise-grade tooling are required. Move quickly on bespoke internal workflows while partnering on more critical, cross-functional processes appropriately.
- **Self-source high-value opportunities:** Work directly with frontline teams and leaders across Sales, CS, and RevOps to identify friction, uncover inefficiencies, and generate a pipeline of projects that materially improve how the business runs.
- **Own outcomes, not tickets:** Drive work end-to-end from problem identification through implementation, adoption, and iteration—with success measured by business impact, speed, and usability.

**Your Expertise**
- **Strong experience building workflows, automations, or internal tools** in GTM, Revenue Operations, and adjacent technical roles, ideally in a high-growth SaaS environment.
- **2+ years of experience working across GTM systems** such as Salesforce, Gong, enrichment tools, and automation platforms, with a strong track record of improving process through systems.
- **Hands-on experience with GTM systems and automation tooling**, such as Salesforce, Gong, Zapier, enrichment platforms, AI workflow tools, or similar technologies.
- **Strong systems judgment**, including the ability to distinguish between workflows that should be solved through fast, bespoke builds versus those that require more durable, enterprise-grade solutions.
- **A high-agency builder mindset:** You are entrepreneurial, resourceful, and comfortable operating off-leash within clear swim lanes. You do not wait for perfect requirements to get started.
- **Demonstrated ability to move quickly and independently**, turning loosely defined business problems into practical, working solutions with limited oversight.
- **Fluency with AI tools and emerging automation capabilities,** along with genuine curiosity about how to apply them in practical ways to improve business operations.
- **Strong cross-functional instincts and communication skills,** with the ability to work directly with technical and non-technical stakeholders and quickly understand where pain exists.

**Compensation**
- The US base salary range for this full-time position is $140,000 - $175,000 annually + equity + benefits.

**Location/Workplace Type**
- United States.

**Role Overview**  
Databahn is looking for a Product Manager – Product Operations to drive operational rigor, pricing strategy, margin optimization, and roadmap governance across our Security Data Fabric platform.  
**This role blends:**  
• Product Operations leadership  
• Pricing and monetization ownership  
• Margin and cost-to-serve visibility  
• Core product management execution  
You will establish strong intake processes, govern roadmap prioritization, track POCs through production, and ensure visibility into cost-to-serve at customer and feature levels—while driving scalable pricing and healthy gross margins.  
This role is critical to ensuring Databahn scales efficiently, profitably, and predictably.  

**Key Responsibilities**  
1. **Product Operations Leadership**  
   - Own the centralized intake process for customer feature requests, sales-driven enhancements, and strategic initiatives.  
   - Define clear evaluation criteria across revenue impact, margin implications, cost-to-serve impact, and strategic alignment.  
   - Establish roadmap governance frameworks and prioritization cadences.  
   - Ensure trade-off transparency across Engineering, Finance, and Sales.  
   - Maintain visibility into committed vs exploratory work.  

   - Define and operationalize a structured POC lifecycle with qualification criteria, success metrics, engineering investment thresholds, and exit criteria.  
   - Track all POCs from inception through technical validation, commercial validation, and production deployment.  
   - Measure conversion rate from POC to production, engineering effort vs revenue realized, and margin impact of custom implementation.  
   - Build frameworks to quantify cost-to-serve across data ingestion, storage, compute, routing & enrichment, and customer-specific configurations.  
   - Develop dashboards to track cost per GB ingested, cost per routing workload, and cost per customer segment.  
   - Partner with Finance to align pricing with infrastructure realities and track gross margin by feature and customer.  

2. **Pricing Strategy & Monetization**  
   - Own Databahn’s pricing and packaging strategy.  
   - Design scalable pricing models aligned to data ingestion volume, throughput, transformation workloads, and infrastructure cost drivers.  
   - Conduct pricing experiments and elasticity analysis.  
   - Partner with Sales on enterprise deal structuring.  
   - Support custom pricing models while protecting margin integrity.  
   - Conduct win/loss analysis with pricing competitiveness insights.  

3. **Margin Optimization**  
   - Analyze cost drivers across data ingestion, storage, compute, and routing and enrichment.  
   - Collaborate with Engineering to improve architectural efficiency, reduce infra spend per workload, and increase automation.  
   - Identify and execute initiatives that expand gross margins.  
   - Track and improve margin performance at feature level, customer segment level, and enterprise account level.  

4. **Core Product Management**  
   - Own roadmap prioritization balancing revenue impact, margin expansion, customer enhancements, and strategic platform investments.  
   - Translate pricing and operational insights into clear product requirements.  
   - Drive structured PRD creation and release documentation.  
   - Use modern AI-assisted tools to accelerate documentation, analyze customer feedback, model pricing scenarios, and summarize operational datasets.  
   - Ensure high execution velocity with operational discipline.  

5. **Customer & Market Engagement**  
   - Work closely with Sales to structure large enterprise deals.  
   - Monitor trends across security data platforms, SIEM vendors, and observability pipelines.  
   - Maintain awareness of AWS, GCP, and Azure cost structures.  
   - Partner with Customer Success on renewal strategy, expansion pricing, and margin protection in upsells.  

6. **Cross-Functional Leadership**  
   - Collaborate deeply with Engineering, Finance, Sales, and Customer Success.  
   - Serve as the internal authority on product monetization, cost-to-serve economics, operational product governance, pricing strategy, and margin health.  

**Minimum Qualifications**  
- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or related field  
- 6+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS, infrastructure, or platform products  
- Experience in Product Operations, roadmap governance, or revenue operations alignment  
- Experience in security, SIEM, or observability platforms  
- Strong analytical skills with experience in pricing and margin analysis  
- Understanding of distributed systems, APIs, and cloud-native architectures  
- Experience owning cross-functional execution across Engineering, Sales, and Finance  
- Strong written communication skills and experience creating PRDs  
- Experience using AI-assisted tools in product workflows  

**Preferred Qualifications**  
- Experience in usage-based SaaS pricing models  
- Experience in observability platforms  
- Familiarity with cloud cost modeling (AWS, GCP, Azure)  
- MBA or background in finance or business strategy  
- Startup experience in high-growth, high-scale environments  

**Why This Role Matters**  
Databahn operates in a data-intensive domain where infrastructure efficiency, pricing precision, and operational discipline directly determine profitability.  
This role ensures:  
- POCs convert into scalable revenue  
- Roadmaps are governed by economic reality  
- Cost-to-serve is visible and optimized  
- Pricing becomes a strategic advantage  
You will help build not just a product—but a financially durable, operationally disciplined platform built for scale.

Plane sells to engineering, product, and IT teams, and to buyers with real compliance and self-hosting needs. These people delete generic outreach on sight. Your job is to make outbound specific enough, timed well enough, and relevant enough that a skeptical technical buyer replies.

- Use LLMs from Anthropic, OpenAI, and others to research accounts and personalize at scale
- Turn Plane's signals into trigger-based plays: GitHub activity, Docker pulls, self-host installs, community engagement, funding, hiring, and tech-stack changes
- Keep the CRM clean and in sync with your data and sequencing layers
- Track reply rate, positive reply rate, meetings booked, pipeline created, and cost per meeting
